Compute the 'prime partition function' Z(beta) = prod_p (1 - e^{-beta log p})^{-1} and show it equals the bulk partition function. Impact: the Riemann Hypothesis is equivalent to a holographic stability condition — zeros on the critical line means the bulk geometry is stable against perturbations.

/-!
# Stability of Sharp Transitions under Bounded Recoding

This file isolates an abstract phase-transition principle for antitone order
parameters on natural-number complexity levels.  Convergence to zero gives a
unique last level at or above every admissible positive threshold.  The main
result shows that replacing the complexity encoding by a monotone cofinal
recoding which moves every level by at most `D` moves the critical index by at
most `D`.

namespace ProofSpacePhaseTransition

open Filter Topology

/-- An antitone real-valued order parameter converging to zero has a unique
critical index at every positive threshold not exceeding its initial value. -/
theorem existsUnique_criticalIndex
    (f : ℕ → ℝ) (ε : ℝ)
    (hanti : Antitone f)
    (hlim : Tendsto f atTop (𝓝 0))
    (hε : 0 < ε)
    (hstart : ε ≤ f 0) :
    ∃! c : ℕ, ε ≤ f c ∧ f (c + 1) < ε ∧
      ∀ n, (f n < ε ↔ c < n) := by
  obtain ⟨N, hN⟩ : ∃ N, ∀ n ≥ N, f n < ε := by
    simpa using hlim.eventually (gt_mem_nhds hε)
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ : ∃ c, ε ≤ f c ∧ f (c + 1) < ε := by
    contrapose! hN
    exact ⟨N, le_rfl, Nat.recOn N hstart fun n hn => hN n hn⟩
  refine ⟨c, ⟨hc.1, hc.2, fun n => ⟨?_, ?_⟩⟩, ?_⟩
  · intro hn
    exact not_le.mp fun h => hn.not_ge (hc.1.trans (hanti h))
  · intro hn
    exact lt_of_le_of_lt (hanti hn) hc.2
  · intro d hd
    grind

/-- **Bounded-recoding stability theorem.**  Let `f` be an antitone order
parameter tending to zero, and let `r` be a monotone cofinal recoding of
complexity levels fixing zero.  If every level is displaced by at most `D`,
then both the original parameter and `f ∘ r` have unique critical indices at
an admissible threshold, and those indices differ by at most `D` in both
natural-number directions. -/
theorem criticalIndex_stable_under_bounded_recoding
    (f : ℕ → ℝ) (r : ℕ → ℕ) (ε : ℝ) (D : ℕ)
    (hfanti : Antitone f)
    (hflim : Tendsto f atTop (𝓝 0))
    (hrmono : Monotone r)
    (hrlim : Tendsto r atTop atTop)
    (hrzero : r 0 = 0)
    (hdisp : ∀ n, n ≤ r n + D ∧ r n ≤ n + D)
    (hε : 0 < ε)
    (hstart : ε ≤ f 0) :
    ∃! p : ℕ × ℕ,
      let c := p.1
      let d := p.2
      (ε ≤ f c ∧ f (c + 1) < ε ∧
        ∀ n, (f n < ε ↔ c < n)) ∧
      (ε ≤ f (r d) ∧ f (r (d + 1)) < ε ∧
        ∀ n, (f (r n) < ε ↔ d < n)) ∧
      d ≤ c + D ∧ c ≤ d + D := by
  obtain ⟨c, hc, hcu⟩ :=
    existsUnique_criticalIndex f ε hfanti hflim hε hstart
  have hcompanti : Antitone (fun n => f (r n)) :=
    fun _ _ h => hfanti (hrmono h)
  have hcomplim : Tendsto (fun n => f (r n)) atTop (𝓝 0) :=
    hflim.comp hrlim
  have hcompstart : ε ≤ f (r 0) := by
    simpa [hrzero] using hstart
  obtain ⟨d, hd, hdu⟩ :=
    existsUnique_criticalIndex (fun n => f (r n)) ε
      hcompanti hcomplim hε hcompstart
  have hdc : d ≤ c + D := by
    have hcr : c < r (c + D + 1) := by
      have := (hdisp (c + D + 1)).1
      omega
    have hlt : f (r (c + D + 1)) < ε := (hc.2.2 _).2 hcr
    have := (hd.2.2 _).1 hlt
    omega
  have hcd : c ≤ d + D := by
    have hle : r (d + 1) ≤ d + D + 1 := by
      have := (hdisp (d + 1)).2
      omega
    have hlt : f (d + D + 1) < ε :=
      lt_of_le_of_lt (hfanti hle) hd.2.1
    have := (hc.2.2 _).1 hlt
    omega
  refine ⟨(c, d), ⟨hc, hd, hdc, hcd⟩, ?_⟩
  rintro ⟨c', d'⟩ hp
  apply Prod.ext
  · exact hcu c' hp.1
  · exact hdu d' hp.2.1

end ProofSpacePhaseTransition

* `goodManifolds_eq_two_pow` — closed form: `goodManifolds n = 2 ^ n` for `n ≥ 7`.

* `goodManifolds_tail_sum` — geometric partial sums of the tail.

  | 3 => 12

  | 5 => 40
  | 6 => 80
  | _ => 0

six dimensions the value is read from `head`; from dimension `7` onward it is
the pure power `2 ^ n`. -/

example : goodManifolds 2 = 8 := by decide

  rw [if_neg (by omega)]

    goodManifolds (n + 1) = 2 * goodManifolds n := by

/-!
# Rooted three-vertex paths in finite simple graphs

This file formalizes the obstruction for the central root of `P₃` highlighted in
*From roots to paths: graphs simultaneously irregular with respect to rooted and ordinary paths*.
For a vertex `v`, a copy of `P₃` rooted at its center is determined by an
unordered pair of distinct neighbors, so its number is `Nat.choose (G.degree v) 2`.
-/

namespace RootedPathIrregular

open SimpleGraph

/-- The number of three-vertex paths whose central vertex is `v`. -/
def centralP3Count {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) [Fintype V]
    [DecidableRel G.Adj] (v : V) : ℕ :=
  (G.degree v).choose 2

/-- Concrete witnesses for central-rooted copies of `P₃`: two-element sets of
neighbors of the root. -/
def centralP3Witnesses {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) [Fintype V]
    [DecidableRel G.Adj] (v : V) : Finset (Finset V) :=
  (G.neighborFinset v).powersetCard 2

/-- The witness interpretation really has the advertised binomial count. -/
theorem card_centralP3Witnesses {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) [Fintype V]
    [DecidableRel G.Adj] (v : V) :
    (centralP3Witnesses G v).card = centralP3Count G v := by
  simp [centralP3Witnesses, centralP3Count,
    Finset.card_powersetCard, SimpleGraph.card_neighborFinset_eq_degree]

/-- A vertex is the center of no three-vertex path exactly when it has
fewer than two neighbors. -/
theorem centralP3Count_eq_zero_iff {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) [Fintype V]
    [DecidableRel G.Adj] (v : V) :
    centralP3Count G v = 0 ↔ G.degree v < 2 := by
  simp [centralP3Count, Nat.choose_eq_zero_iff]

/-- In every finite simple graph with at least two vertices, the degree map
fails to be injective. This is the familiar pigeonhole obstruction sharpened by
the impossibility of having both an isolated and a universal vertex. -/
theorem degree_not_injective {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (hV : 2 ≤ Fintype.card V) :
    ¬ Function.Injective (fun v => G.degree v) := by
  intro hinj
  -- If degree is injective, the n vertices map to n distinct values in {0, ..., n-1}
  -- This means all values 0 to n-1 are used, including both 0 and n-1
  -- But degree n-1 means adjacent to all other vertices, contradicting degree 0 existing
  have hn : Fintype.card V ≥ 2 := hV
  haveI : DecidableEq V := Classical.decEq V
  -- Each degree is bounded by n - 1.
  have hdeg_bound : ∀ v : V, G.degree v < Fintype.card V := fun v => by
    have h2 : v ∉ G.neighborFinset v := by simp [SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset]
    have hcard_erase : (Finset.univ.erase v).card = Fintype.card V - 1 := Finset.card_erase_of_mem (Finset.mem_univ v)
    have hsub : G.neighborFinset v ⊆ Finset.univ.erase v := by
      intro x hx
      rw [Finset.mem_erase]
      exact ⟨fun heq => h2 (heq ▸ hx), Finset.mem_univ x⟩
    have : G.degree v ≤ Fintype.card V - 1 := by
      simp only [SimpleGraph.degree]
      exact Nat.le_trans (Finset.card_le_card hsub) hcard_erase.le
    linarith [Nat.sub_add_cancel (by linarith : 1 ≤ Fintype.card V)]
  -- The degrees form a Finset in Fin (Fintype.card V) with cardinality n
  -- So all values 0 to n-1 are used
  -- There exist vertices with degree 0 and degree n-1, which is a contradiction
  -- Consider the image as a subset of Fin (Fintype.card V)
  let f : V → Fin (Fintype.card V) := fun v => ⟨G.degree v, hdeg_bound v⟩
  have hf_inj : Function.Injective f := by
    intro a b hab
    simp only [f, Fin.mk.injEq] at hab
    exact hinj hab
  -- The image of f has cardinality = Fintype.card V = card of Fin n
  -- So f is surjective
  have hf_surj : Function.Surjective f := (Fintype.bijective_iff_injective_and_card _).mpr ⟨hf_inj, by simp⟩ |>.2
  -- So there exist vertices with degree 0 and degree n-1
  -- Get vertex with degree 0
  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := hf_surj ⟨0, Nat.zero_lt_of_lt hn⟩
  -- Get vertex with degree n-1
  obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := hf_surj ⟨Fintype.card V - 1, Nat.sub_lt (by linarith) (by linarith)⟩
  simp only [f] at hu hv
  simp only [Fin.mk.injEq] at hu hv
  -- u has degree 0, v has degree n-1
  -- v with degree n-1 is adjacent to all other vertices
  -- but u with degree 0 is adjacent to no vertices, including v
  by_cases huv : u = v
  · -- If u = v, then degree u = 0 = n - 1, so n = 1, contradicting n ≥ 2
    rw [huv] at hu
    omega
  · -- If u ≠ v, then v is adjacent to u (since degree v = n-1)
    -- but u is not adjacent to v (since degree u = 0)
    have hvad : G.Adj v u := by
      have huniv : G.neighborFinset v ⊆ Finset.univ.erase v := fun x hx =>
        Finset.mem_erase_of_ne_of_mem (fun heq => by rw [heq] at hx; rw [SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset] at hx; exact G.irrefl hx) (Finset.mem_univ _)
      have hcard_erase : (Finset.univ.erase v).card = Fintype.card V - 1 := Finset.card_erase_of_mem (Finset.mem_univ v)
      have heq_finset : G.neighborFinset v = Finset.univ.erase v := by
        apply Finset.eq_of_subset_of_card_le huniv
        simp [hv]
      rw [← SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset]
      exact heq_finset ▸ Finset.mem_erase.mpr ⟨huv, Finset.mem_univ u⟩
    -- Since Adj is symmetric, G.Adj u v
    have hvu : G.Adj u v := G.symm hvad
    -- But degree u = 0 means u has no neighbors
    rw [SimpleGraph.degree, Finset.card_eq_zero] at hu
    rw [← SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset] at hvu
    rw [hu] at hvu
    simp at hvu

/-- No finite simple graph on at least two vertices has pairwise distinct
central-rooted `P₃` counts. This is the nonexistence theorem for nontrivial
`(P₃)ᵣ`-irregular graphs when the root is the central vertex. -/
theorem not_centralP3_irregular {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (hV : 2 ≤ Fintype.card V) :
    ¬ Function.Injective (centralP3Count G) := by
  intro hinjective
  have hnotdeg := degree_not_injective G hV
  rw [Function.Injective] at hinjective hnotdeg
  push_neg at hnotdeg
  obtain ⟨u, v, hdeg, huv⟩ := hnotdeg
  exact huv (hinjective (by simp [centralP3Count, hdeg]))

/-- Equivalently, every finite simple graph on at least two vertices contains
 two distinct vertices lying centrally in the same number of `P₃` copies. -/
theorem exists_distinct_equal_centralP3Count {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (hV : 2 ≤ Fintype.card V) :
    ∃ u v : V, u ≠ v ∧ centralP3Count G u = centralP3Count G v := by
  have h := not_centralP3_irregular G hV
  simp only [Function.Injective] at h
  push_neg at h
  obtain ⟨u, v, huv, hne⟩ := h
  exact ⟨u, v, hne, huv⟩

end RootedPathIrregular
